title: Gamma Automation: How to Use the API (2026 Guide)
summary: Gamma automation with the API creates presentations programmatically without the UI. See the available endpoints and how to authenticate your calls.
body_markdown:
## Frequently asked questions


Someone sends a request and gets back a refusal that has nothing to do with their payload. Each of these questions starts there.


### Is Gamma's API available on the free plan?


Yes: API access is available on all plans, including Free, though limits differ, so a free account's plan limits are worth checking when a request is rejected.


On a free account, a connector can still show its Gamma action, and the action then fails at run time. Seeing the action in a menu doesn't prove your plan can call it. Read the plan comparison on Gamma's pricing page before you build anything.


### Can Gamma automatically update an existing deck?


The generation API is documented as creating a new deck on each call, not editing one in place. So a "refresh the weekly report" automation produces a fresh deck with a fresh link every run.


Unless you store the returned link somewhere your team looks, such as a spreadsheet row or a channel message, **people keep opening last week's version** . If Gamma's docs add an edit endpoint, that changes this answer, so check them.


### Does Gamma automation work with Zapier or Make?


Yes, both automation platforms offer Gamma connectors, and both do the same job as a direct API call. The connector sends the generation request with the fields you fill in. It's therefore bound by the same plan, credit and input limits as your own script.


When a Zap or scenario run fails, you are usually looking at the API's error message passed through, so open the run history and read the response body before changing the workflow.


### How many credits does one generated deck use?


It depends on the deck, and Gamma's pricing and credits documentation is the only place to get the current numbers. Cost varies with how much you generate and with which image model you choose, since some image models cost more per image than others.


When a trigger fires on every new row, it can drain a monthly balance faster than a person clicking "generate" ever would. Run the test request, check the balance afterward, and multiply by your expected volume before you switch the trigger on.


### Can I automate export to PDF or PowerPoint?


Yes, in the sense that the generation request can ask for a file export alongside the deck, and the response returns a link to download it. Check the current API reference for the exact parameter name and the formats it accepts.


The export link is the output you pass to the next step, such as emailing a client or filing it in a folder. Treat that link as something to fetch promptly, not a permanent address, unless the docs say otherwise.
